rules.statement: Validate an issuer that is configured or stored as an absolute `https` URL (`http` only for a loopback host) that has no user information, query, fragment or whitespace and is bounded in length.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Discovery section 3 and RFC 8414 section 2 require this issuer form. An issuer that breaks it publishes a discovery document that conforming clients reject.
rules.check: Look at code that accepts an issuer from configuration or an API request. Report it when it doesn't reject non-https schemes for non-loopback hosts, userinfo, a query, a fragment, whitespace, or unbounded length.

rules.statement: Never reissue an issuer or tenant identifier once it is retired: when a tenant is deleted or gives up its issuer, record a tombstone in the store layer in the same unit of work, and only the former holder may take back a retired issuer.
rules.why: Relying parties key their trust by the issuer string. A reused issuer or name would let a new tenant mint tokens that clients trusting the old tenant accept. Retiring in the store, not in an endpoint, means seeders, importers and other callers can't bypass it.
rules.check: Look for tenant delete or issuer-change paths that free an identifier or issuer without writing a tombstone in the same transaction, retiring that happens only in an API endpoint, validation that lets a retired identifier or issuer be taken, and any API that releases a retired issuer.

rules.statement: Route every write path for a value through one shared validation seam that pluggable implementations extend, instead of copying the rules into an API layer or branching on built-in implementation codes.
rules.why: A second copy of the rules drifts from the first. Branching on built-in codes closes an open vocabulary, so custom implementations can't take part.
rules.check: Look for validation logic duplicated between startup options validation and an API validator, and for switch or if chains on built-in strategy or provider codes inside shared validation.

rules.statement: When options validation depends on a pluggable implementation, have each implementation register its own `IValidateOptions<T>` that skips when it isn't the selected one, and keep only the shared checks in the common validator.
rules.why: A custom implementation can then validate its own options the same way the built-in ones do, and the common validator never has to know every implementation.
rules.check: Look for a single `IValidateOptions<T>` that validates each built-in implementation's settings by switching on the selected code.

rules.statement: Report validation failures as structured results that tell a value invalid on its own apart from a conflict with another resource, and answer `400` for invalid values before `409` for conflicts.
rules.why: A caller has to tell a malformed value (`400`) apart from one that another resource holds (`409`), and plain messages can't express that.
rules.check: Look for validators that return plain strings for both kinds of failure, endpoints that map every failure to one status code, or endpoints that check conflicts before value validity.

rules.statement: On update, revalidate an address-like field against the current configuration only when the update changes it, not on every update.
rules.why: A record written under an earlier configuration could otherwise never have unrelated fields, such as its display name, edited.
rules.check: Look for update validators that run the full address or configuration-dependent validation even when the request doesn't change those fields.

rules.statement: Validate a caller-chosen tenant identifier as a lowercase RFC 1123 host label (1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens that start and end with a letter or digit) wherever it enters, including configured identifiers at startup, and keep it out of update requests so it can't change.
rules.why: That one form works as a path segment and as a host label under every tenant strategy, so a tenant's issuer is known before the tenant exists. The identifier is part of the immutable issuer.
rules.check: Look for tenant identifier inputs (create requests, configured root or static tenant IDs) that skip this validation or accept mixed case, and for update contracts that carry the tenant identifier.
